item.title: Military to aid Manitoba First Nation hit by power outage, frozen pipes
item.description: PIMICIKAMAK CREE NATION, MAN. — The federal government has agreed to send in military help to a northern Manitoba First Nation where thousands have been forced to leave due to frozen pipes and sewage backup.

item.title: Saskatoon hospital patient dead after altercation with security
item.description: SASKATOON — Police in Saskatoon are investigating after a patient died Friday at the Royal University Hospital following an altercation with security.

item.description: Boy, 10, found dead inside Tamarack Woods home New Year's Eve after officers attended for wellness check

item.title: 'Old gal has had rough night': Main break floods iconic Yukon bar amid -40 C weather
item.description: A major water main break in Dawson City, Yukon, flooded streets and a historic bar as temperatures plunged to -40 C amid a recent cold snap.

item.title: Judge reserves ruling on whether to throw out B.C. murder conviction over delays
item.description: VANCOUVER — A British Columbia Supreme Court judge has reserved her decision on whether to throw out the case against a man convicted of first-degree murder in a killing police have linked to organized crime.

item.title: Judge says Trump administration can’t block child care, other program money for 5 states for now
item.description: A federal judge ruled Friday that President Donald Trump's administration cannot block federal money for child care subsidies and other programs aimed at supporting low-income families with children from flowing to five Democratic-led states for now.

item.title: Alberta's Smith calls on Carney to speed up major project approvals
item.description: EDMONTON — Alberta Premier Danielle Smith is calling on Ottawa to further speed up its approval process for major projects, saying she wants to see applications green-lit within six months.

item.title: Newcomers should be primed for Quebec winter roads after 2025 fatal crash: coroner
item.description: MONTREAL — A Quebec coroner is recommending the province's auto insurance board better prepare newcomers about the dangers of winter driving, following the death of a Mexican man last year.
